en: Having bowed down to the illustrious Gaṇeśa, who has attained the perfection of learning, and by the great grace of the divine Sūryanārāyaṇa,
I— the learned Bhaṭṭa of Kanyāpura— shall expound the characteristics of the vowels of ritual action (kriyā), just as [it was taught] by him. 1.
Therefore, when the four others took away the first [portion] which possessed the initial udātta accent, Tvaṣṭṛ gave him the barley; therefore, he said to him, "You are indeed the supreme one.
He entered him, and he spoke to him in such a way as Soma had brought forth.
They caused [him] to enter, they took it, they employed it, and by that there was a *mindā*;
there was *māyā*; he took the *kumbhī*; "there is" (*asti*) preceded by *syat*; from *bha* and from *āśaya*, the former and *paribhūr asi* beginning with *sā*. 3–4.
Where Indra hears me, where he gathers [the wood], and where he sprinkles his own head— here,
the words *atra* and *ādi* are accented acute (udātta).
Furthermore, the word *tho* is acute, as is everything following the word *yat*.
The remaining accents should be understood by the wise through the *saṃhita* accent as well.

Wherever there is a word ending in *yat*, *yāvat*, *yatra*, *yathā*, *yadi*, *yatas*, *yadā*, *yarhi*, *hi*, or *adhas*, the first syllable from the twelfth preceding one receives the *udātta* (acute) accent due to its connection with the action (*kriyā*).
Those subjects who have passed away, those two vital breaths (prāṇa) which are superior—just as Soma went forth three times today, so has he driven away the cold.
That [cup] belonging to Mitra and Varuṇa, that indeed is it; and that which belongs to the axle, and that which belongs to Agni.

For these [verses] are known as the *vidhi* (prescriptive formulas); however, when one performs the *citi* (piling) again, [one uses] "Life indeed is another," and so forth, or "This Soma belongs to Varuṇa.
One should not perform [the rite] with the formula "To thee, for the earth," even in the case of Soma, nor even with the previous one.
He places the calf [on the fire] until the end; he does not [recite] before the rising of the *puroḍāśa*.
For one of low caste, it begins with *apayusmat* and ends with *āvartata*;
it is not [to be recited] by one who is hungry, nor by one who has consumed Soma, nor by Agni before the assembly.

Agni was in yonder [heaven] among the gods, and there were three joints in the cow; Soma and Agni alone were for him above, by means of the boneless and the true; the Ādityas were in yonder [heaven], and the milk of the unshakable one—the Viśvedevas stood by that.

In the prima facie argument (*pūrvapakṣa*), [the words] *vā* and *anya* [apply]; likewise, up to the fifth [verse], the left [hand] does not [perform the rite], nor the sacrifice, nor the wealth; twice [he is] not led away, nor is he freed from debt (14).
[He is] barley, [he is] the Saudāsas, [he is] the high, and in those [verses] following the chariot wheel.
The connection [of the *yajus*] occurs when there is proximity at the end; for two equal [units], the first is the higher one.
"Mayati," "vaṣaṭ," "stṛṇute," "tṛtīya," "urundhe," "eva ca," "yunakti," "prajāpate," "asya," "pāhi," and so forth, as well as the beginning of a *yajus*, [mark the end]. 15–16.

One should not kill the bull; the two-fold ritual does not apply to those who follow other scriptures, just as Manu and his descendants [do not]. Just as there are those who live by sacrifice, so too [are there others]. With the head and so forth, Dhruva, the saline soil (ūṣā), the downward-flowing [substances], the clarified butter (ājya), and the loose earth (purīṣa).
The embers are from the Aruṇa bamboo; the sacrificial altar is that which is beyond [the world];
having invoked the gods for himself, the heavenly world comes from the horse, and the two eyes from Rudra. For he who is made of clay holds aloft what is entirely below. 18–19.

In another city and not in another, if one thing is placed before another; having begun with what is to be maintained, that word stands in the middle, lowly. Even in the word for number, it does not end in "na"; there is no single group of eight due to proximity.
Even in the case of the unprecedented (*apūrva*), the action is eternal; thus stands another Yajus verse beginning with "nityam.
For not he, for that, for those, for her—for her is illusion (*māyā*), for it is so;
they go, let them go; he who is in her; that which belongs to them, and indeed here.
"Whoever shall sacrifice," "for whomsoever," "in this manner," "with such effort," "to whatever extent," and "whoever"—
these [terms] are indeed described as being for the purpose of indicating the essential nature (*svarasa*) for the sake of beginners;
thus ends the section on the basis of attainment (*prāptimūla*).
